text:
jordan_customer: Hi, we're seeing streaming responses from the Python SDK that cut off early and the async iterator reports one less message than the server sent. billing spike too. Anyone seen this?

alex_support: sorry to hear that — can you paste a minimal repro and a request_id?

jordan_customer: request_id: req_20260315_9ab3. Repro is basically: start a stream, consume iterator until StopAsyncIteration, but sometimes final chunk never yields and iterator returns early. Using async for chunk in client.stream(...):

jordan_customer: ```py
async for event in client.stream("/v1/chat/stream", json={"model":"gpt-open-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"long convo"}]}, stream=True):
    if event.type == "message":
        print(event.text)
    if event.type == "done":
        print("DONE")
```

jordan_customer: Observed: sometimes no "DONE" and iterator stops, total printed message count is N-1. Also billing shows tokens for that missing chunk intermittently.

alex_support: thanks — can you confirm SDK version and whether you're using `asyncio` on Windows or Linux?

jordan_customer: python-sdk 0.6.4, linux, uvloop. Happens ~1/50 streams, non-deterministic. Happened after we upgraded from 0.6.2.

meera_dev: @alex_support @jordan_customer filing a quick try: can you set env REDWOOD_SSE_DEBUG=1 and re-run to capture raw frames? we had a recent change around stream close handling.

jordan_customer: attached raw frame snippet: 

jordan_customer: ```
frame: data: {"id":1,"type":"message","text":"..."}
frame: data: {"id":2,"type":"message","text":"..."}
frame: data: 


frame: event: close
```

jordan_customer: you can see an empty data line before the close event. iterator seems to treat that as EOF.

alex_support: :eyes: good find. @meera_dev any recent changes parsing blank data lines?

meera_dev: quick note — we adjusted the SSE parser to trim trailing newlines to avoid spurious empty events, but IIRC there was an off-by-one where a blank `data:
` before `event: close` could get treated as an empty payload and trigger the iterator to finish. I'll run local tests.

ryan_sdk: pinging in — I remember a regression in 0.6.4 where `__anext__` returned StopAsyncIteration if an empty data frame was seen right before `event: close`. That would explain missing final chunk and inconsistent billing. Will repro.

meera_dev: repro script I'm running locally:

meera_dev: ```py
import asyncio
from redwood_sdk import AsyncClient

async def fake_server_stream(writer):
    writer.write(b'data: {"id":1,"type":"message","text":"one"}\n\n')
    await writer.drain()
    writer.write(b'data: {"id":2,"type":"message","text":"two"}\n\n')
    await writer.drain()
    # intentional blank data line
    writer.write(b'data:\n\n')
    await writer.drain()
    writer.write(b'event: close\n\n')

# use a local http server to stream the above, then client.stream(...) and iterate
```

meera_dev: results: on 0.6.4 my iterator yields id 1 then stops. on 0.6.2 it yields both then DONE.

alex_support: ok escalating to eng-runtime. tagging @ryan_sdk to include the regression range and a proposed fix. Do you have a minimal bindable test we can run in CI?

ryan_sdk: created a tiny pytest + asyncio test to simulate the sequence. patch candidate: treat empty `data:` frames as no-op rather than end-of-stream; ensure we wait for explicit `event: close` before StopAsyncIteration. I'll open a PR and include the test.

jordan_customer: thanks — how fast can we get a fix? this is causing billing noise and dropped user messages.

meera_dev: I'll try to get hotfix in next patch release. if you can, downgrade to 0.6.2 as a temporary mitigation. also enabling REDWOOD_SSE_DEBUG helps us see frames.

ryan_sdk: PR posted: https://git.redwood.ai/p/redwood/sdk/pulls/1425 (internal). patch changes sse/parser.py: treat `data:` with empty payload as skip. added test `test_empty_data_before_close`.

deploy-bot: deploy initiated: sdk-canary/0.6.5-hotfix -> canary (sha: bc9f3d)

alex_support: we'll keep monitoring req_20260315_9ab3 and similar ids. jordan_customer if you can run canary or wait for 0.6.5 release we'll follow up. :thumbsup: 

jordan_customer: can confirm applying the patch locally fixes our repro. thanks everyone! :tada:
